name: stb_zip (CRC32 routine)
workload: CRC32 checksum of a 1GB in-memory buffer
claimed_speedup: CRC32 of 1GB data: 0.2 sec (stb_zip) vs 1.1 sec (miniz 3.0) = 5.5x
tradeoffs: Header-only single-file C library; only supports store/deflate ZIP entries, not a general-purpose zlib replacement.
caveats: First-party single-table README benchmark; miniz is a widely-used lightweight zlib-compatible library but is not the canonical zlib CRC32 baseline itself, and compiler/flags are unstated.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): HN Algolia search "crc32 zlib"

verification.tier_reason: The README's BENCHMARKS table (Core i7-12700K, 32GB RAM) states 'CRC32 of 1GB data | 0.2 sec | 1.1 sec | 5.5x' vs miniz 3.0. The repo has only README.txt, LICENSE and stb_zip.h: no benchmark code, compiler or flags, so these are numbers without methodology.
verification.notes: The README numbers exist but belong to a different checksum. The only fast path computes CRC-32C, which is wrong for ZIP. The IEEE CRC-32 path matches miniz's byte-table algorithm, so the project is not actually faster at the baseline's function. It is also only 8 stars with 4 commits, all on 2025-08-13. Metadata checked: MIT, not a fork, not archived, stale (last commit 2025-08-13).

name: turbobase64 (Cython/Python bindings for Turbo-Base64)
workload: Python-level base64 encode/decode of byte strings, dispatching at runtime to scalar/SSSE3/AVX/AVX2/AVX512-VBMI C kernels
claimed_speedup: "20-30x faster than the standard library"; "Benchmarks faster than any other C base64 library" (per project's own benchmark.py chart)
tradeoffs: Adds a Python/Cython layer over the underlying C SIMD kernels; the "faster than any other C library" claim is only presented as a chart image, not tabulated numbers, in the README.
caveats: The underlying SIMD codec is powturbo/Turbo-Base64, which is already catalogued (excluded per KNOWN_LIST); this entry's distinct contribution is the separate Python/Cython binding repo and its own comparative benchmark, not new SIMD code. No CPU/compiler stated.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): HN Algolia search "fastest base64 library"

verification.tier_reason: The README states '20-30x faster than the standard library'. Its chart (from benchmark.py, timeit over os.urandom inputs) plots only Python's base64.b64encode against the project's own scalar/SSSE3/AVX/AVX2/AVX512 encode paths. There is no CPU, compiler or flag detail, so this is first-party C tier.
verification.notes: This is really the known-list project powturbo/Turbo-Base64 (https://github.com/powturbo/turbo-base64) repackaged as a Python binding with a prebuilt libtb64.a. The binding could at most be mentioned on the Turbo-Base64 entry. Metadata checked: GPL-3.0, 15 stars, last commit 2023-08-07 (abandoned), not a fork, not archived.
